plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (Chirped Depth-Graded Stack) based on feedback to implement monotonicity-enforcing thickness parameterization. Three complementary routes: (1) direct refinement with cumulative exponential mapping to enforce air-to-substrate increasing thickness regime, (2) reduced-layer periodic stack (20 layers) to test if fewer layers improve convergence while maintaining dual-band performance, (3) hybrid topology separating UV-reflection chirped section from SWIR-transmission quarter-wave section. All routes preserve the 30-layer maximum constraint and HfO2/SiO2 material restriction.

routes.title: Monotonicity-Constrained Chirped Stack with Cumulative Exponential Mapping
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Enforcing monotonic thickness progression via cumulative exponential parameterization (t_i = t_base + Σ exp(ξ_j)) will reduce optimizer degrees of freedom, smooth the loss landscape, and improve convergence compared to unconstrained chirped optimization, while maintaining the depth-graded principle for broadened UV reflection band.
routes.design_principle: Chirped distributed Bragg reflector with monotonically increasing optical thickness from air to substrate to broaden the UV reflection band (300-450 nm) while maintaining SWIR transmission (1000-1700 nm) through reduced index contrast at longer wavelengths.
routes.proposed_topology: 30-layer chirped stack: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_15 | Fused Silica substrate. Layer sequence starts with HfO2 at air interface, alternates HfO2/SiO2, ends with SiO2 at substrate interface for environmental durability.
design_variables: 15 cumulative exponential thickness parameters (ξ_j) for bilayer pairs
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability per evidence
theory_basis: Chirped DBR theory for bandwidth broadening
Cumulative exponential mapping for monotonicity enforcement
expected_advantages: Smoother optimization landscape due to reduced effective DOF
Maintains route_02's chirped principle while addressing numerical convergence issues
known_risks: Monotonicity constraint may limit optimal solutions if non-monotonic thickness profile is actually superior
Cumulative parameterization may introduce numerical stiffness if ξ_j values span large ranges
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 chirped multilayer coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)/SiO2(2)/HfO2(3)/SiO2(4)/HfO2(5)/SiO2(6)/HfO2(7)/SiO2(8)/HfO2(9)/SiO2(10)/HfO2(11)/SiO2(12)/HfO2(13)/SiO2(14)/HfO2(15)/SiO2(16)/HfO2(17)/SiO2(18)/HfO2(19)/SiO2(20)/HfO2(21)/SiO2(22)/HfO2(23)/SiO2(24)/HfO2(25)/SiO2(26)/HfO2(27)/SiO2(28)/HfO2(29)/SiO2(30). Implement monotonicity-enforcing parameterization: define each layer thickness t_i = t_base + cumulative_sum(exp(ξ_j)) for j=0 to i, where ξ_j are the optimizable parameters and t_base is a fixed offset. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximum reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer (layer 30) thickness >= 200 nm for environmental durability. Use gradient-based optimizer with the monotonicity mapping to reduce effective degrees of freedom. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Direct refinement of route_02 implementing feedback directive: monotonicity-enforcing variable mapping via cumulative exponential parameterization to constrain optimizer to physically required air-to-substrate increasing regime, reduce effective DOF, and smooth loss landscape for faster gradient descent convergence.

routes.title: Reduced-Layer Periodic Stack for Improved Convergence
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 30 to 20 layers will improve numerical convergence by reducing optimization dimensionality while maintaining sufficient bandwidth for UV reflection (300-450 nm) through optimized quarter-wave pair thicknesses, with SWIR transmission preserved by the inherent transparency of HfO2/SiO2 materials in 1000-1700 nm band.
routes.design_principle: Periodic quarter-wave Bragg reflector optimized for UV band center (~375 nm) with non-quarter-wave adjustments to broaden reflection band, leveraging the natural SWIR transparency of the material pair.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer periodic stack: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_10 | Fused Silica substrate. Alternating HfO2/SiO2 bilayers with optimized thicknesses, ending with SiO2 at substrate.
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Minimize total coating thickness for stress reduction
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 20 (well within <=30 constraint)
Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability
Reduced layer count improves deposition repeatability
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to reduced optimization dimensionality (20 vs 30 variables)
Lower total thickness reduces stress and deposition time
Tests whether 30 layers are necessary or if 20 layers suffice for dual-band performance
known_risks: 20 layers may not provide sufficient UV reflection bandwidth compared to 30-layer chirped design
Periodic structure may have narrower reflection band than chirped approach
May require thicker individual layers to compensate for fewer pairs
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 periodic multilayer coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)/SiO2(2)/HfO2(3)/SiO2(4)/HfO2(5)/SiO2(6)/HfO2(7)/SiO2(8)/HfO2(9)/SiO2(10)/HfO2(11)/SiO2(12)/HfO2(13)/SiO2(14)/HfO2(15)/SiO2(16)/HfO2(17)/SiO2(18)/HfO2(19)/SiO2(20). Initialize thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness at 375 nm (UV band center): HfO2 ~50 nm, SiO2 ~65 nm, then allow full optimization. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximum reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer (layer 20) thickness >= 200 nm for environmental durability. Use gradient-based optimizer with bounded thickness variables (10-300 nm per layer). Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Alternative approach to route_02's convergence issues: reduces layer count from 30 to 20 to decrease optimization dimensionality while testing whether periodic quarter-wave structure can achieve comparable dual-band performance to chirped design. Addresses numerical_convergence failure category from route_02.

routes.title: Hybrid Chirped-Periodic Stack with Band-Separated Sections
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Separating the coating into two functional sections - a chirped UV reflector (layers 1-14) optimized for 300-450 nm reflection and a quarter-wave SWIR transmitter (layers 15-28) optimized for 1000-1700 nm transmission - will improve dual-band performance by allowing independent optimization of each band's requirements while maintaining monotonic thickness progression overall.
routes.design_principle: Hybrid topology: front section (air-side) uses chirped DBR for broadband UV reflection, rear section (substrate-side) uses quarter-wave matching for SWIR anti-reflection, with monotonic thickness transition between sections.
routes.proposed_topology: 28-layer hybrid stack: Air | [Chirped HfO2/SiO2]_7 pairs (layers 1-14) | [Quarter-wave HfO2/SiO2]_7 pairs (layers 15-28) | Fused Silica substrate. Ends with SiO2 for durability.
design_variables: 14 chirped section thicknesses with monotonicity constraint
14 quarter-wave section thicknesses with band-specific optimization
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Minimize reflection ripple in SWIR band
Ensure smooth thickness transition between sections
manufacturing_considerations: Outermost SiO2 layer (layer 28) >= 200 nm for environmental durability
Section-based design may simplify process control
expected_advantages: Independent optimization of UV reflection and SWIR transmission requirements
Chirped section broadens UV reflection band
Quarter-wave section minimizes SWIR reflection losses
Hybrid approach may outperform single-topology designs
known_risks: Interface between sections may create unwanted reflection peaks
28 layers approach the 30-layer limit, leaving less margin for optimization
Section boundary may cause numerical discontinuities in optimization
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 28-layer HfO2/SiO2 hybrid multilayer coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)/SiO2(2)/HfO2(3)/SiO2(4)/HfO2(5)/SiO2(6)/HfO2(7)/SiO2(8)/HfO2(9)/SiO2(10)/HfO2(11)/SiO2(12)/HfO2(13)/SiO2(14)/HfO2(15)/SiO2(16)/HfO2(17)/SiO2(18)/HfO2(19)/SiO2(20)/HfO2(21)/SiO2(22)/HfO2(23)/SiO2(24)/HfO2(25)/SiO2(26)/HfO2(27)/SiO2(28). Section 1 (layers 1-14): chirped DBR optimized for 300-450 nm reflection with monotonically increasing thicknesses. Section 2 (layers 15-28): quarter-wave stack optimized for 1000-1700 nm transmission with thicknesses near quarter-wave at 1350 nm (SWIR band center). Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximum reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer (layer 28) thickness >= 200 nm for environmental durability. Use gradient-based optimizer with section-specific initialization and bounds. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Complementary approach to route_02: instead of uniform chirped topology, separates coating into functionally distinct sections to independently optimize UV reflection and SWIR transmission. Tests whether band-separated optimization outperforms unified chirped approach while still addressing convergence through section-specific parameterization.
